bath.prompt: Make a new picture of a different room. Nothing from the attached bedroom appears in the new picture: no bed, no pillow, no blanket, no rug, no shelf, no door. Use the attached bedroom picture only for its soft 3D art style, its warm night lamp light and its camera height and distance: a small child standing on this floor must come out the same size as on the bedroom floor. Draw a small cozy bathroom at night, seen straight from the front. The back wall is warm cream tiles with one soft lavender stripe of tiles at the height of the sink's rim, and the floor is light warm-beige tiles: no green, no mint and no light blue anywhere in the room. A low rounded white pedestal sink stands against the back wall on the left half of the picture, its rim at about a small child's chest height; on the sink's rim there is only one small plain lavender cup, nothing else. The wall above the sink is plain tiles with one small round warm glowing wall lamp: no mirror, no cabinet, no shelf. A small round window on the right part of the back wall shows a dark blue night sky with a crescent moon and a few stars. A soft peach towel hangs on a hook on the back wall between the sink and the window. The tiled floor is open and empty from the middle to the right, with room for a child to stand just right of the sink and plenty of air above. The bottom-right corner is plain tiled floor. No bathtub, no toilet, no rug, no people, no animals, no toys, no text. Make the picture 4:3 and keep the sink, the window, the towel and the open floor in the middle part of the picture, away from the edges.

props_truth.note: Every thing is seen from the same angle: from the front, slightly from above. No faces on the table, the vases, the flowers, the cups or the heart; only the two germs have their own little face. The three vases are the very same vase at the same size; the two cups are the very same cup at the same size; the two germs are the very same germ at the same size; the flowers are the very same three flowers every time. Every vase is whole: no cracks, no broken pieces. Sizes compared with the bedside table: the vase is about half as tall as the table, and its round belly is about two fifths as wide as the table's top; the flowers' stems are about as long as the vase is tall, so in the vase the blooms reach about half the vase's height above its rim; the cup is about half as tall as the vase and a little narrower, so the vase and the cup fit side by side on the table's top; the spilled vase with its puddle is about one and a half times as wide as the table; the loose flowers are about as long as the vase is tall; each germ and the heart are about as big as the cup.
